newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Ariane rocket to launch two satellites for Asia.
newsitem.headline: Ariane rocket to launch two satellites for Asia.

text.p: Western Europe's 95th Ariane rocket is scheduled to blast off from French Guiana on Wednesday carrying two satellites to service Asia, the Arianespace company said on Monday.
The Thaicom 3 satellite will provide voice, data and video services throughout Asia for the Bangkok-based Shinawatra Satellite Company. It was built by France's Aerospatiale.
The BSAT-1a satellite, built by Los Angeles-based Hughes Space & Communications, will be used for direct television broadcasting over Japan.
An Ariane 44LP rocket is due to lift the two satellites, which have a combined weight of 3.9 tonnes, into space.
The launch is set for between 7.59 p.m. and 8.41 p.m. (2259 and 2341 GMT) from the European Space Agency (ESA) centre in Kourou, French Guiana, on the northeast coast of South America.
The Paris-based Arianespace company leads the commercial satellite launch market. It has successfully placed 18 heavy satellites into orbit with the use of 12 Ariane rockets since January 1996.
The company said it had firm orders to launch another 41 satellites worth an estimated $3.5 billion.
